commits.message: fix(load-gate): the budget check is unjudged under snapshots; the snapshot wait and NODE_OPTIONS form live in the lib; the fold's memory line states a consequence (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)
fix(scripts): a snapshot is matched by V8's name shape, the wait reuses sleep, NODE_OPTIONS is quoted; the fold's key comment says why the stamp is left out (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)

fix(load-gate): re-derive the budget from CI with every built-in placed (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)

Measured on PR #622's CI: 186 MB charged once collected at 20 sessions (feed criterion, feed off) and 514 MB at 100 (load gate). per-session = (514 - 186) / 80 = 4.1 MB, base = 186 - 20 * 4.1 = 104 MB, headroom a fifth as before. The gate placed neither metrics nor activity when the old 112 + 3.1 MB were measured.

fix(facts): one transcript fold in flight per session; the gate places every built-in and can snapshot its heap (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.c0y)

The 100-session gate failed with metrics and activity on because the
transcript fold started a new fold for every request of a session while
the session's first fold was still out, and a cold fold re-enters the
8-slot read gate once per window: folds arrived faster than any could
finish, none landed, the stamp fast path never engaged, and every
request's refresh stayed alive in the queue. The fold now coalesces per
session through the same SingleFlight the usage store's request refresh
uses.

The gate's config places metrics, activity, tokenSparkline and
autocompact, so it gathers every built-in the facts epic makes
always-on. `--heap-snapshots DIR` has the daemon write its heap at the
two collections through Node's signal snapshot; the whole-file wait
moves from capture-heap into scripts/lib and both call it.
test: lower the daemon-boot ratchet to 201, the cases left after the load-config e2e blocks went

review(medium): drop the request facts an open failure kept for the removed follow; the design docs say load-config is gone

The open-failure entry carried the request facts so a click that moved
the origin could reopen by them; with the follow gone nothing reads
them, so the entry is the error alone. The home spec and the isolation
survey no longer list load-config as work to do.

review(high): one report shape for a template's issues; the retired-URL check says what it reads; keep the flag-over-hint coverage

- cross-ref: the three places that reported a template's issue at the helper
  or the declaration collapse to one local report; the retired-verb loop is
  one line of it.
- The retired-verb check reads every string literal, not only a link
  argument, so its comment and message say 'spells', not 'links to'.
- scheme.ts states the real one-way-deps reason: the codec imports config
  modules, so config must not import the codec.
- Restore the e2e coverage that the deleted pick test carried along:
  --config outranks the configEnv hint, and an empty flag is no flag.
- Drop the stale load-config lines in the design docs and a render-cache
  comment that still named a click as a view mover.

feat(click)!: remove the load-config verb; a session's config is what its request names (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.f00.bju)

The verb that pointed a session at any absolute path goes, with the
per-session override it wrote, the "pick" arm it added to a session's
config target, and the view-follow hook that ran after every click
because a click might have moved the origin. Nothing but a render
request sets a session's origin now, so the render, every durable click
and the lane meter read the recorded origin directly.

A config that still writes a `cc-candybar://load-config/…` link is
refused at load, at the template or the helper that spells it, with a
message naming --config and CC_CANDYBAR_CONFIG as where a session's
config comes from. The scheme string moves to a leaf module so the
loader can read it without the config layer depending on the click
codec.

BREAKING CHANGE: the load-config click verb and the examples' config
switcher are removed; a config linking to the verb fails to load.

feat(tmux-status): the renderer names itself on every session whose row it draws (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.rwj) (#619)

* feat(tmux-status): the renderer names itself on every session whose row it draws (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.rwj)

The install plan's lay-out write sets `@cc-candybar-renderer` on the tmux
session in the same call as the prior record and the status-format array,
and the restore plan unsets it beside the prior and wrote records. The name
reaches the lane through its deps; the composition root passes `main`, the
main renderer's name, until the home lane carries a name. The install log
line says which renderer laid the session out.

Proved on a private tmux server: the option reads `main` while the row is
drawn, SIGTERM returns the session's options to what they were, and a second
daemon started after that names itself on the row again.

* fix(tmux-status): a layout taken over names this daemon too, as a fresh one does (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.rwj)

Every install plan carries its commands, so the write after it has no branch:
a taken-over record gets the renderer option, and so does each layout the
first answer adopts from the server's listing. The option's comment names
what it is for rather than a binding that does not exist yet. The unit test
file carries only the ticket's change, not a reformat. The process test's
setup is back under its try so a tmux refusal still cleans up.

* refactor(tmux-status): the taken-over install plan derives from the record it extends (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.rwj)

## [1.190.0](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/compare/v1.189.0...v1.190.0) (2026-11-05)

### Features

* **apply:** the closed Event union and its one arm table (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.scr) ([#618](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/618)) ([6e15ada](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/6e15adacbcc9130dc4d651aec67c94627d9e7680))
test(apply): the apply-update case holds its own turns for the holder; doctor-menu reads the latest doctor line, since the apply line now follows every click (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.g2l)

feat(apply): a click's launches are effects, performed after its turn and reported as effect-done (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.g2l)

A handler describes what it asks of the world (a program, a line typed
into its pane, the update's act) as an Effect and awaits no child. The
arm table answers `{ answer, effects }`; `apply` performs the effects
in order after the arm and puts each outcome back through the new
effect-done arm, which holds a failed one for the session's bar in a
turn of its own. One `apply` log line per click, menu-idle and
effect-done event names the verb, the effects and the revision.

typeSlash takes a TmuxHint: the pane's absence is refused at the click,
the pane's own refusals are the effect's failure. A rate-limited click
launch is a failed outcome shown in the bar, no longer a silent ack.

Tests: the click helper drives Apply and installs a store view that
throws on a write made with no turn held; cases that parked a pbcopy to
hold the turn park a doctor gather instead.
test(facts): name the doctor's closure tests for what they protect (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)
fix(facts): the wait's comment names every session; the doctor's namespace-read test returns (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)

chore(facts): delete the wants closure (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)

The facts document is total, so the question "which fields does this config
read" has no caller with a reason. Every session now gathers every built-in:
git runs one constant option set (forge lookup included), every declared
plugin source is held, and burn, block and autocompact's context cap are always
composed. A view's declaration depends on the request alone, so a preset pick
moves no hold.

Deleted: the wants function, the needed-prefix builders, the sources-read walk,
the closure parameter through declare/refresh/read/project, the PR reads gate,
the git options derived from the closure, `Gathered`, `declaredSources`, and the
view's preset reaction. The doctor's data-needs walk stays and now owns its own
per-segment path closure, since it answers what a config would read.

The bar is byte-identical; the payload golden gains the keys that were gated
(block, burn, metrics, activity, tmux and the like on presets that did not read
them). Tests that asserted gating are deleted; the fold-edge cases they covered
(partials, helpers handed a dict) move to the doctor's path closure.
